6054.t: Of foreign origin, perhaps connected to πάρδαλις (párdalis).

6060.t: Traditionally explained (such as by Frisk) as a derivative from πέρδομαι (pérdomai, “to fart”), due to the droning sound when partridges take wing.

6058.t: Uncertain. Some suggest the source is Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂- (“flat, broad, plain”), whereas others such as Beekes suggest a non-Indo-European origin.

6084.t: The suffix "-αρνο-" suggests a Pre-Greek origin.

6049.t: From Proto-Indo-European *(ts)ptyew- (“to spit, vomit”). Akin to Latin spuō, Albanian pështyj, Old English spīwan (English spew), Old Armenian թուք (tʻukʻ), Old Church Slavonic пльвати (plĭvati), Sanskrit ष्ठीवति (ṣṭhīvati).

6087.t: From Proto-Indo-European *tworHos (“seizer, encloser”), from Proto-Indo-European *twerH- (“to enclose”). Cognate to Proto-Slavic *tvȏrъ (“creature”) and Proto-Slavic *tvoriti (“to make”).

6050.t: From Proto-Indo-European *pewǵ- (“to punch”). Cognates include Latin pugnus, Lithuanian puši̇̀s, and Old English fyst (English fist).

6082.t: From either σκεῦος (skeûos, “vessel”) or σκευή (skeuḗ, “equipment”) + -άζω (-ắzō), both ultimately of the same origin.

6094.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *sper- Proto-Indo-European *-yeti Proto-Indo-European *spéryeti Proto-Hellenic *spéřřō Ancient Greek σπείρω (speírō) Proto-Hellenic *-ā́ Ancient Greek -α (-ā) ? Proto-Indo-European *sper- Proto-Indo-European *-h₂…

6086.t: According to Beekes, the phonetic variants listed above in the "Alternative forms" section prove Pre-Greek origin for this word.

6067.t: The etymology is uncertain. Maybe related to σήθω (sḗthō, “to sift, bolt”) or perhaps a contamination of σαπρός (saprós, “rotten”) with an unknown word.

6071.t: Clearly related to σέλμα (sélmă, “deck of a ship”). These words have been compared to Old English selma and syll, and to German Schwelle (“threshold”), but phonetically this etymology is unconvincing.

6097.t: From the root of στείβω (steíbō, “to tread on, stamp on”).

6076.t: Possibly a loanword from Egyptian šnḏwt (“kilt”). Compare also Hebrew סָדִין (sadin, “bedsheet”).

6096.t: From *σπάργω (*spárgō, “to swaddle”), which is from the zero-grade of Proto-Indo-European *sper- (“to twist”) with a g-extension (perhaps via contamination with a verb of similar meaning, like εἴργω (eírgō, “to enclose”)).

6095.t: From σπάω (spắō, “to draw (a weapon)”) + -ων (-ōn, nominal suffix).

6005.t: From the root of ποιμήν (poimḗn, “shepherd”) + -η (-ē), from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂- (“to protect, shepherd”).

6085.t: Perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kelH- (“to cut”) (whence σκάλλω (skắllō, “to stir up; to search”)), although the vowel is hard to explain. Unrelated to σκῦτος (skûtos, “hide, skin”).
